title: Hotel Key Cards Vs Hotel Wristbands
summary: Hotels rarely choose between cards and wristbands on aesthetics alone. The better decision usually comes from guest flow, property type, amenity access and how many credentials the staff can realistically issue and recover.
heroPoints: Cards are still the default for room access at most properties.
Wristbands gain value when guest convenience and amenity access matter more.
Mixed programs work when the property accepts a more deliberate issuance workflow.

rows: Easy to issue, familiar for guests, scalable across properties
More loss risk and less convenient in pools or wet environments
Hands-free use, harder to lose, strong guest segmentation potential
Sizing, material and compatibility questions come earlier
Properties with separate room and amenity logic
Can optimize convenience without replacing every credential path
More complex issuance and inventory management

sections.title: What usually decides it
sections.intro: The choice usually gets clearer once the property describes how guests move, what environments dominate and how many access scenarios the staff has to support.
bullets: Resorts, water environments and child-focused properties often gain more from wristbands.
Properties with tiered amenities may use cards for rooms and wristbands for zones or packages.
Premium material choice matters after the format decision, not before it.

faq.question: Are wristbands replacing hotel cards everywhere?
faq.answer: No. Wristbands are gaining ground in resort and amenity-heavy contexts, but cards remain the default in many standard room-access programs.

faq.question: When is a mixed program worth it?
faq.answer: When the property has clearly different room and amenity workflows and can manage a more deliberate issuance process.
